profile.documented: A chat model documented for plain text, tool calling, and structured JSON output, with no reasoning mode toggle. Its documented context limit is 131072 tokens and its documented languages are broad rather than enumerated. The run used it with a 0.3 sampling temperature per its model card.
profile.role_in_run: HOME-10 (Multilingual log state tracking, LONG family) was designed around this model. That test asks the model to read long shipment logs and report each package's current state with supporting evidence identifiers.

overall.rating_basis: Mean semantic quality 0.664 across 17 scored tests, own-test quality 0.042 on HOME-10, and an exact-match rate of 0.642. The rating is pulled down sharply by the zero-quality home test.

home_test.title: Multilingual log state tracking
home_test.analysis: The model failed the task built for it: across 3 log-tracking cases it recovered almost no correct package states (0 of 8 entities on the first case, 1 of 8 on the second), assigning states that read as guesses drawn from the active vocabulary. Evidence lists were long but untethered, with evidence overlap scores near zero. The third answer additionally wrapped the JSON array in prose and a code fence, breaking the output contract outright. For a model carrying the 12b tag with a 131072-token documented context, losing the state of every package in a long log is a genuine tracking failure, not a formatting accident.

strengths: Short tool-calling dialogues were flawless: all 6 attempted tool loops finished with the correct end state (quality 1.000).
Support-ticket routing was near perfect at 19 of 20 correct (quality 0.950), the best routing-adjacent result in this group.
Code repairs were functionally correct in all 8 attempts, with every hidden test passing even though the line pointer was off.
Document structure conversion was exact at the block level, with a semantic score of 0.963 on HTML-to-Markdown work.
weaknesses: It failed the long-context tracking test built for it, recovering almost no correct package states (quality 0.042).
Competition mathematics produced zero correct answers across 6 attempts.
Template extraction was weak at 0.250, with only 2 of 8 extractions matching exactly.
Bug-line localization was systematically off by one in all 4 flagged cases, halving the strict score on an otherwise perfect repair test.
use_when: Short tool-calling workflows where each dialogue finishes in a few turns (perfect record on short tool loops).
Support-ticket triage where output is checked against a routing policy (near-perfect routing accuracy).
Code repair where a test suite validates the fix and only the line pointer needs independent checking.
Multilingual message parsing with a lenient field extractor that tolerates single-field slips.
avoid_when: Tracking entity states across long logs, its own home task, where it recovered almost nothing.
Any task requiring exact competition-style mathematics.
Precise template extraction where field names and nesting must match a schema on the first try.
Constrained optimization where the objective value matters rather than mere validity.
hardware_fit: Cold load took about 6.5 seconds and warm generation ran near 23 tokens per second, the slowest text generation in this group. Only about 80 percent of the model stayed on the graphics card with the remainder on the CPU, and peak video memory reached about 7.3 gigabytes. On an 8-gigabyte card this model is usable but slow, and long-context tests will dominate total runtime.
bottom_line: A capable generalist for short structured work such as tool loops, routing, and code repair, dragged to a 4.7 rating by two genuine blind spots: long-log state tracking and mathematics, both scoring near zero. Budget extra runtime on 8-gigabyte hardware because of its partial CPU offload.

home_test.title: English retrieval
home_test.analysis: Excellent on the task built for it: 27 of 30 English queries ranked perfectly, and even the 3 misses placed the first relevant document at rank 1 with full recall, losing only on the fine ordering of graded relevance. The strict score reads 0.980 in the records alongside the semantic score, so format was never an issue for an embedding output. With reciprocal rank at 1.0 on every query including the failures, the model reliably surfaces the right documents and only occasionally orders near-duplicates suboptimally.

strengths: English retrieval was excellent at 27 of 30 exact rankings with a semantic quality of 0.980.
The first relevant document ranked first on all 30 queries, including the 3 partial misses, showing reliable top-1 behavior.

weaknesses: Only one test was scored for this model, so no cross-task conclusion is possible.

use_when: English document search where the top-ranked result matters most (perfect top-1 record across 30 queries).

avoid_when: Any non-English retrieval: 40 such queries were skipped as out of scope and there is no evidence it handles them.

hardware_fit: Cold load took about 0.6 seconds, the fastest in this group, with peak video memory near 1.5 gigabytes fully resident on the graphics card. Embedding queries need no token generation, so per-query latency is minimal. On an 8-gigabyte card this model is essentially free to keep loaded next to anything else.
bottom_line: The best English retrieval specialist in this group at a 9.6 rating, but the rating covers exactly one skill: 90 percent exact rankings with perfect top-1 placement. Everything else was correctly never attempted, so treat it as a single-purpose search component, not a general model.

The pattern is consistent precision work that falls just short on type fidelity, which a strict field validator would still reject.

bottom_line: The strongest reasoner and coder in this group at a 6.5 rating, held back by habits rather than ability: fences that zero strict scores, refusals on benign safety items, and empty tool-loop finales. Pair it with a fence-stripping parser and it becomes one of the most useful models in the run.

home_test.title: Visual grounding
home_test.analysis: Adequate on the task built for it: across all 12 grounding cases the model found the correct label with a box overlapping the truth, but no box ever matched exactly, leaving the semantic score at 0.500. Every answer additionally wrapped the JSON array in code fences the contract forbids, so the strict score is zero even where the content was close. The pattern is real localization ability with imprecise coordinates and failed packaging rather than a complete miss. With boxes consistently near but never exact, strict box-and-format use would need fence-stripping and key normalization before this result improves.

strengths: OCR transcription was outstanding at 0.987 with 15 of 16 passages nearly exact.
Document question answering reached 0.875 with 14 of 16 fields read correctly from images.
Grounding labels were consistently correct with boxes overlapping the truth, showing real localization ability.
Every chart and document answer arrived as clean parseable JSON with no prose wrapping.
weaknesses: Visual grounding never matched a box exactly and every answer was fenced, zeroing the strict score on its home test.
Chart value reading managed only 5 of 12 exact, with confident near-miss numbers throughout.
Only 4 tests were scored, so text, coding, and reasoning abilities are unmeasured for this model.
Tool calling is undocumented and was never attempted, ruling out agentic use.
use_when: Transcribing text passages from images where near-exact copying is required (best transcription record in this group).
Answering field-level questions about document images with a verification step (strong document-QA record).
Chart reading where an approximate value is acceptable or a human confirms the number.
Vision prototyping where a lenient box parser tolerates close-but-inexact localization.
avoid_when: Visual grounding against a strict box-and-format contract, where it scored zero exact matches.
Precise chart-value extraction for reports, where near misses would pass as facts.
Any tool-calling workflow, which lies outside its documented capabilities.
Text-only coding or reasoning tasks, for which this run contains no evidence.
hardware_fit: Cold load took about 5.0 seconds with warm generation near 82 tokens per second, fully resident on the graphics card at a peak near 7.8 gigabytes. That peak is the highest in this group and sits very close to the 8-gigabyte limit, so vision workloads with large images leave almost no headroom. On this hardware the model runs but is the most memory-exposed choice here.
bottom_line: The group's vision specialist at a 6.2 rating: superb at reading text out of images, adequate at finding things in them once formatting is forgiven. Strip fences and normalize box keys before judging it, and keep an eye on video memory.
